result.summary:
REQ-VALIDATOR round 3, REQ-001 and REQ-007 together: FAIL on one blocking finding, R3-1: AC14 still claims «ничего не исключено и ничего не пропущено», but three demonstrated ways around the one check pass every AC14 guard. All five round-2 findings (N1-N5) are resolved. The analyst's replacement rule for N1 is sound, and better than my round-2 example. Two more findings are minor: R3-2 misstates the rule's tie limitation, and R3-3 is a missing journal-size bound. All three fixes are small and dry-run below. Design must not start. Next: REQ-ANALYST (third rework), then re-validation.

What I validated: docs/requirements.yaml, sha256 e3ff122583913d071c224461cbcc7f9cfd906e2904fbf622a68f480f86a28cb2, 618 lines. REQ-001 block b4cf9bc0..., REQ-007 b0a739b4... — both equal the analyst's values. Protected parts are unchanged:
- REQ-005 and REQ-006, via REQ-006 AC14's awk: 33 lines / 44463bb3... and 148 lines / b958eb67....
- Header 007174d5...; REQ-002..REQ-005 71f5be84....
Against my round-2 copy (c170e322...), only these changed:
- REQ-001: description and AC1-AC4, AC6, AC8, AC14;
- REQ-007: description, AC1 and AC6.
original_request is unchanged in both.

ROUND-2 FINDINGS
- N1 resolved; the new rule is sound.
  - AC4 (б) is a symmetric conflict rule. (в) is the clock rule, now used only for the last line. AC2 fixes that lines are appended in acceptance order, and adds 20 concurrent writes at ±59 s that must stay unmarked.
  - I re-ran both analyst simulations (readrule-sim.mjs, readrule-sim2.mjs); the outputs are exactly as reported. Under the analyst's reading of my round-2 example, real lines are marked in the back-dated cases. The deviation was right.
  - I then wrote my own implementation from the AC4 text (scratchpad/val-r3-rule.mjs):
    - honest journals: 600 lines in 5 gap regimes (0 s to 2 h), ±59 s offsets, 20% at the extremes: 0 marks;
    - back-dated forgeries (dense, sparse, after a single line, far past): only the forged line is marked;
    - the same journal read at T and at T+2 h: identical marks;
    - a +1 h line followed by 2 or more real lines: only it is marked.
  - Proof sketch: accepted lines A before B satisfy A.at <= t_A+60 and B.at >= t_B-60 >= t_A-60, so no conflict is possible.
- N2 resolved. The session-end rules are now positional in both requirements:
  - REQ-001 AC6(в): «после её начала … событие окончания её сессии»; AC6(г) the same;
  - REQ-007: «последнее событие которого — не событие окончания сессии».
  Fact 12 checks out against the live docs: cli-reference, --fork-session; hooks, SessionStart «resume» covers --resume, --continue and /resume; SessionEnd reason resume. Both test lists add the end, resume (same session_id), start sequence.
- N3 resolved for config blocks. From tools/, the rules print-config gives 856ee001... (23 files, 1 distinct line) and the globals command gives bec0f88d...; both match. Probes on a scratch copy:
  - `"no-undef": 0` in the base rules changes the rules hash (3f65dfcb);
  - the allowed files+globals block for public/ keeps both hashes, and eslint passes.
  Other mechanisms of the same class remain open: see R3-1.
- N4 resolved. The REQ-007 AC6 grep (-i, plus javascript:) on samples: clean 1; onClick 0; javascript: 0; attribute on its own line 0; missing folder 2. REQ-001 AC8 and REQ-007 AC6 require src on every <script> in served HTML (server test).
- N5 resolved. AC3 names SessionStart's own source field as never sent, and each documented example must give exactly one journal line, including SessionStart.

NEW - BLOCKING
R3-1 - REQ-001 AC14 (Q4, Q6; same class as m2 and N3, AP-014). I should have listed the whole class in round 2. Three changes weaken the one check and still pass every AC14 guard. I demonstrated each on a scratch copy of sai/ and restored it afterwards.
  (a) A narrowed npm script in tools/package.json, the very file this run edits. With "lint" limited to `eslint src/cli.js --max-warnings 0`, npm run check exits 0 on a file with a lint error; the original scripts give 1. The devDependencies and lockfile pins do not change.
  (b) A prettier config. A "prettier": {"requirePragma": true} key in package.json, or a .prettierrc in tools/ or in sai/, makes prettier --check . exit 0 on an unformatted file; without it, 1. The .prettierignore pin does not change.
  (c) An inline ESLint rule comment. `/* eslint no-undef: 0 */` lets eslint pass on browser code (`document`) with no globals block. Both print-config hashes are unchanged, because --print-config does not see inline comments, and both greps exit 1.
Fix (each dry-run):
  - Replace the devDependencies pin with `jq -S -c 'del(.scripts."pixel-office")' tools/package.json | shasum -a 256` = 5c59292586d92e95c1ea507ef7a46790a125677172c3fe3abfd90dedd9edf0a4. Only the pixel-office script may be added; this covers scripts, devDependencies, engines and a prettier key.
  - From tools/, `npx prettier --find-config-path src/pixel-office/<any file>; echo $?` must give 1. Today it prints «Can not find configure file» with exit 1; it prints package.json or ../.prettierrc when either exists.
  - Widen the directive grep to `grep -rnE 'eslint-disable|/[*][[:space:]]*eslint[[:space:]]|prettier-ignore' tools/src/pixel-office tools/test; echo $?`, which must give only 1. It is backslash-free, so safe in a YAML double-quoted string; it parses in ruby YAML. It exits 1 on today's tools/src and tools/test. It catches `/* eslint no-undef: 0 */`, `/*eslint no-undef:0*/` and every eslint-disable form, and ignores `/* global document */`. It works with ugrep and BSD grep.

NEW - MINOR (fix in the same rework)
R3-2 - REQ-001 description «Где что лежит» (R2). The tie sentence «несколько вписанных строк «из будущего» до прихода такого же числа настоящих строк уводят пометку на настоящие» understates the rule's own behaviour. My simulation (cases B and C) shows three things.
  - One forged line is enough: k = 1 with one real line.
  - Real lines stay marked while m <= k. Here m counts the real lines in the window, meaning earlier than the forged time minus 120 s. So for k = m the real lines are still marked; they are released only at m = k+1, not «when the same number arrives».
  - Real lines later than the forged time minus 120 s never conflict with it. So the wrong state is permanent when no more real lines fall into the window. B3/B4: a +5 min forged line, one real line in the window, then five real lines after it; the real line stays marked and the forged line counts, at any read time. B6 is the same with +1 h and an hour of silence.
Fix: state this exactly, and add it to the tools/README.md «### Ограничения» list (AC13 grep). Also say in (б) that a marked line drops out of the conflicts. An alternative for ORCH: mark both lines of a tied pair. Then a line known to be in conflict is never counted, at the cost of hiding the real line in a sparse back-dated tie. Either way, the text must match the rule.
R3-3 - REQ-001 AC4 and AC7: no journal-size bound. The page applies the rule to the whole journal on every update (5 s at most, AC7), and rotation is out of scope. A literal pairwise implementation measured (Node 22) 23 ms at 5,000 lines, 313 ms at 20,000 and 1,285 ms at 40,000 — quadratic, about 8 s at 100,000. The small-fixture tests would pass it. Fix: a page test on a generated journal, e.g. 100,000 accepted lines plus a variant with a few hand-written ones, in which the read rule and the task list take at most 1 s. Or state the complexity: an honest journal needs one pass, since a conflict exists iff some line is more than 120 s earlier than the maximum time before it.
